pr_title: rtio: Use an atomic completion counter
pr_body:
Rather than looking at the pool of completions for spinning use an atomic counter of total completions ever done. The relative number of completions being waited on by rtio_submit may then always be correctly done.

Prior to this a race was possible, and understood, as rtio_cqe_consumable was a likely but not guaranteed count of completions. Sure enough on an SMP system the likely count was ahead of the actual available completions and a race was caught by the simple test case.

Fixes #59715

issue_context.title: rtio: Submit wait count without semaphore may race on smp
issue_context.body:
On certain platforms with multiple cores (smp) rtio_submit(r, 1); rtio_cqe_consume(r); may race as the consumable completion count vs the submit count isn't properly tracked.

Instead a total number of produced completions should be tracked and used to monitor the submit wait count.

On submit the current count is acquired and the desired count waited for.
On completion the count is incremented.

No subtraction should ever take place to avoid a race.
